reader.requirement: At --std 85 a MOVE whose identifier-1 or any identifier-2 is an index data item (USAGE INDEX, standalone, subscripted table element, or a group member named directly) must be refused at compile time, as sender and as receiver, with every literal or figurative sender, while a group that merely contains an index item (MOVE, MOVE CORRESPONDING, reference modification) is not an index data item operand and is admitted.
reader.edition-search: MoveOperandClassChecks is commented and coded version-invariant; grep of MoveTable16.cs for DialectLevel|Edition.Year|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior: no match; the edition-banded MOVE rules (§2023:14.9.25.3 SR5 figurative rows) live in VersionConformancePass and do not touch the index class
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers the index-name operand; index data items as sender and receiver, subscripted index items, a second receiver and the group-containing-an-index admission were not exercised by it

reader.notes: One class reader (IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOf through MoveTable16.SenderClassRefusal / ReceiverClassRefusal) refuses an index-class operand in either position at every edition. The 2023 rule also bars message-tag, object and pointer classes, which cannot be declared at 85, so the shared arm does not over-reject there. Diagnostics cite §2023:14.9.25.3 SR1 at --std 85 (cosmetic).

refuter.evidence: Attacked group-level USAGE INDEX and RENAMES of an index item. Probes at --std 85: r6gidx (01 G USAGE INDEX with 05 I1, I2; MOVE G TO X and MOVE X TO G) -> admitted, OK: G is a group item, not an index data item, because USAGE at group level applies to each elementary item (§1985:VI.5.14.4 GR1); r6gidx2 (MOVE I1 of that group) -> COBOL0809; r6ren (66 RI RENAMES an index item, MOVE RI) -> COBOL0809; r6rm (MOVE IX(1:2)) -> COBOL1647 refused. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.19.3 SR4 'An index data item must not appear as an operand'; OK §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR5 'An index data item can be referenced explicitly only'.
